definition_en: a very small living thing that can cause disease
core_image: 显微镜下一颗会游动的杆状小东西
scene: 实验室的镜片下出现一小片灰色。A single bacterium can divide within minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 bacterium 是「细菌」（第 1 个义项：极微小的单细胞生物）；句意是一个细菌几分钟内就能分裂。

derivatives.zh: 拉丁复数形式，义为「细菌（复数）」
由 bacterium 加 -al 构成，义为「细菌的」
由 bacterio- 与 -logy 构成，义为「细菌学」

senses.title: A single microbe
senses.definition: a very small single-celled living thing, some of which cause disease
senses.definitionCN: 极微小的单细胞生物，有些会致病
senses.example: A single bacterium can divide within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 一个细菌几分钟内就能分裂。
senses.why: Bacterium is Latin for a little rod, the shape early microscopists saw, so the scientific name began as a description of form.
senses.whyCN: bacterium 在拉丁语中意为「小杆」，是早期显微镜观察者看到的形状，所以这个学名起初是对形态的描述。

senses.title: A cause of infection
senses.definition: a bacterium that infects the body and causes illness
senses.definitionCN: 侵入人体并引起疾病的细菌
senses.example: One bacterium was enough to spoil the sample.
senses.exampleCN: 一个细菌就足以让样本坏掉。
senses.why: Because some species cause disease, the singular often appears in medical writing about infection.
senses.whyCN: 由于某些种类会致病，单数形式常出现在讲感染的医学文字中。

intro.en: Bacterium is a scientific name taken from a Greek word for a rod.
intro.cn: bacterium 是一个取自希腊语「杆」的学名。

items.en: bakterion meant 'a small rod'.
items.cn: bakterion 意为「小杆」。

items.en: scientists used bacterium for rod-shaped microbes.
items.cn: 科学家用 bacterium 指杆状微生物。

items.en: English borrowed the singular form.
items.cn: 英语借入了这个单数形式。

items.en: the Latin plural became the everyday word.
items.cn: 拉丁复数成了日常使用的词。

items.en: Bacterium is now mainly scientific.
items.cn: 如今 bacterium 主要用于科学语境。

note.en: The look-alike group is the scientific family; the near-meaning group gives everyday words for tiny organisms.
note.cn: 形近组是科学词族；近义组是日常说法中的微小生物。

normalIntro.en: Bacterium names one rod-shaped cell; bacteria names many.
normalIntro.cn: bacterium 指一个杆状细胞，bacteria 指许多个。

normal.en: The plural is bacteria, not bacteriums.
normal.cn: 复数是 bacteria，不是 bacteriums。

normal.en: The adjective is bacterial.
normal.cn: 形容词是 bacterial。

normal.en: The stress falls on the second syllable: bac-TE-ri-um.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节。

normal.en: A bacterium is a single cell, so it is not visible to the eye.
normal.cn: 一个细菌只有一个细胞，所以肉眼看不见。

normal.en: Not every bacterium causes disease.
normal.cn: 并非每个细菌都会致病。

abstract.cn: 想象镜片下一根游动的小杆。

abstract.en: See one dot splitting into two.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小点分裂成两个。

abstract.en: See a grey smear on a glass slide.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃载片上的一小片灰色。

examples.cn: 一个细菌几分钟内就能分裂。

examples.en: One bacterium was enough to spoil the sample.
examples.cn: 一个细菌就足以让样本坏掉。

examples.en: Each bacterium in the sample was counted.
examples.cn: 样本中的每一个细菌都被计数了。

dict_mnemonic.text: bacterium 像个「小杆」：显微镜下一根会动的小棍，就是单个细菌。

root: 源自希腊语 bakterion「小杆」，经现代拉丁语 bacterium 进入英语，因早期显微镜下细菌多呈杆状；复数保留拉丁形式 bacteria。

sensesIntro.en: One rod-shaped cell and the many it belongs to are the same word at two grammatical numbers.
sensesIntro.cn: 一根杆状细胞与它所属的群体，是同一个词的两种语法数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tiny rod swimming under a lens.
core.cn: 核心意象：镜片下一根游动的小杆。

intro.en: The Greek root bacterion, 'little rod', also gives bacteria and bacterial.
intro.cn: 希腊词根 bacterion 意为「小杆」，也构成 bacteria 与 bacterial。

latinIntro.en: Modern Latin took the Greek diminutive and gave English the pair bacterium and bacteria.
latinIntro.cn: 现代拉丁语借入这个希腊指小词，给英语留下 bacterium 与 bacteria 这对形式。

definition_zh: 坏的；糟糕的；变质的；严重的；有害的
definition_en: not good, or harmful and unpleasant
core_image: 一只苹果从里往外烂了一块
scene: 摊主把那筐水果挪到一边。The milk had gone bad in the heat.
sceneCN: 这里 bad 是「变质的」（第 2 个义项：食物腐坏不能吃）；句意是牛奶在高温下变质了。

pos.zh: 形容词：坏的；糟糕的；变质的；严重的

derivatives.zh: 由 bad 加 -ly 构成，义为「糟糕地；非常」
由 bad 加 -ness 构成，义为「坏；恶劣」
比较级形式，义为「更坏的」

senses.title: Not good
senses.definition: of poor quality or not satisfactory
senses.definitionCN: 质量差或不令人满意的
senses.example: It was a bad idea from the start.
senses.exampleCN: 这从一开始就是个坏主意。
senses.why: Bad is an old English word whose origin is uncertain, and its oldest recorded sense is simply 'inferior'.
senses.whyCN: bad 是古英语词，来源不明，最早记录的义项就是「较差」。

senses.title: Spoiled
senses.definition: no longer fresh or safe to eat
senses.definitionCN: 不再新鲜或不能安全食用
senses.example: The milk had gone bad in the heat.
senses.exampleCN: 牛奶在高温下变质了。
senses.why: Food that has lost its quality is bad in the same way as a bad plan, so the word covers rot as well as failure.
senses.whyCN: 食物失去品质，和糟糕的计划一样都是 bad，所以这个词既指腐坏也指失败。

senses.title: Serious or severe
senses.definition: serious or severe in degree
senses.definitionCN: 程度严重或剧烈
senses.example: She caught a bad cold last winter.
senses.exampleCN: 她去年冬天得了重感冒。
senses.why: Something bad can be not only wrong but large in force, which produced the sense of severity.
senses.whyCN: 坏的东西不仅可能不对，也可能来势很猛，这就产生了「严重」的义项。

senses.title: Harmful
senses.definition: damaging to health or success
senses.definitionCN: 对健康或成功有害的
senses.example: Too much sugar is bad for your teeth.
senses.exampleCN: 糖吃太多对牙齿有害。
senses.why: If a thing is not good for you, it works against you, so bad came to mark harm as well as poor quality.
senses.whyCN: 如果某物对你没好处，它就在跟你作对，所以 bad 也标记伤害，而不只是质量差。

intro.en: Bad is a native English word whose deeper origin is unknown.
intro.cn: bad 是英语本族词，更早的来源并不清楚。

items.en: bad already meant 'poor in quality'.
items.cn: bad 已经表示「质量差」。

items.en: It widened to moral faults.
items.cn: 它扩展到道德上的过失。

items.en: bad covered spoiled food and severe illness.
items.cn: bad 涵盖食物变质与病情严重。

items.en: It became one of the most general negative words.
items.cn: 它成为最通用的否定词之一。

items.en: Bad is also slang for 'very good'.
items.cn: 如今 bad 还有「非常棒」的俚语义。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one vowel; the near-meaning group gives shades of poor and harmful.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个元音；近义组是表示差与有害的词。

a small new shoot of a plant

normalIntro.en: Bad covers quality, freshness, severity and harm.
normalIntro.cn: bad 涵盖质量、新鲜度、严重程度与伤害。

normal.en: The comparative is worse, not badder.
normal.cn: 比较级是 worse，不是 badder。

normal.en: The superlative is worst.
normal.cn: 最高级是 worst。

normal.en: Go bad is used mostly for food.
normal.cn: go bad 多用于食物变质。

normal.en: Bad for you means harmful to you.
normal.cn: bad for you 意为对你有害。

normal.en: Not bad is a mild compliment.
normal.cn: not bad 是温和的称赞。

abstract.en: See a plan falling apart on a desk.

abstract.en: See a dark cloud over a picnic.
abstract.cn: 想象野餐上方的一片乌云。

examples.cn: 这从一开始就是个坏主意。

examples.cn: 牛奶在高温下变质了。

examples.en: Too much sugar is bad for your teeth.

dict_mnemonic.text: 一个短促的 bad：苹果烂了一块，事情办砸了，都叫 bad。

root: 源自古英语 bad「质量差的」，词源不明；中古英语扩展至道德与身体缺陷，近代又涵盖食物变质与病情严重。

sensesIntro.en: Poor quality, rot, severity and harm are four shades of one negative judgment.
sensesIntro.cn: 质量差、腐坏、严重与有害，是同一个负面判断的四种色调。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an apple rotting from the core.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只从果核开始烂的苹果。

intro.en: Bad has no productive affixes, but it supplies the comparative worse and the adverb badly.
intro.cn: bad 没有能产的词缀，但提供比较级 worse 与副词 badly。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base here; the word is native English with an uncertain origin.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，这个词是英语本族词，来源不明。

definition_en: in a poor way, severely, or very much
core_image: 一辆自行车歪倒在路边，轮子还在转
scene: 雨后的路面又滑又亮。He badly wanted to finish the race.
sceneCN: 这里 badly 是「非常」（第 3 个义项：表示程度很强烈）；句意是他非常想跑完这场比赛。

pos.zh: 副词：糟糕地；严重地；非常

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词，义为「坏的」，badly 由其加 -ly 构成
由 bad 加 -ness 构成，义为「坏；恶劣」

senses.title: In a poor way
senses.definition: in a way that is not good or skillful
senses.definitionCN: 以不好或不熟练的方式
senses.example: The team played badly in the second half.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队下半场打得很糟。
senses.why: Badly is bad plus -ly, and its first job is to describe an action done without skill or success.
senses.whyCN: badly 是 bad 加 -ly，最初用于描述缺乏技巧或没有成功的动作。

senses.title: Severely
senses.definition: to a serious or severe degree
senses.definitionCN: 达到严重或剧烈的程度
senses.example: He was badly hurt in the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 他在那次摔倒中受了重伤。
senses.why: A bad injury is a severe one, so the adverb came to mean severely when it describes damage.
senses.whyCN: bad injury 是严重的伤，所以副词在描述损害时就表示「严重地」。

senses.title: Very much
senses.definition: very much or strongly
senses.definitionCN: 程度很深或很强烈
senses.example: He badly wanted to finish the race.
senses.exampleCN: 他非常想跑完这场比赛。
senses.why: Wanting something in a bad way is wanting it intensely, which is how badly became an intensifier.
senses.whyCN: 以很糟的状态想要某物，就是极想要，badly 由此变成了程度副词。

intro.en: Badly is the adverb built on bad.
intro.cn: badly 是建在 bad 上的副词。

items.en: bad meant 'poor in quality'.
items.cn: bad 意为「质量差」。

items.en: bad widened to moral and physical faults.
items.cn: bad 扩展到道德与身体缺陷。

items.en: badly meant 'in a poor way'.
items.cn: badly 意为「以糟糕的方式」。

items.en: It also meant severely and very much.
items.cn: 它也表示「严重地」与「非常」。

items.en: Badly need is a common phrase.
items.cn: badly need 是常见搭配。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ly ending; the near-meaning group gives degrees of poor and severe.
note.cn: 形近组都以 -ly 结尾；近义组是表示差与严重的词。

entries.definition: in a plain and direct way

normalIntro.en: Badly measures poor skill, severe damage or strong desire.
normalIntro.cn: badly 衡量的是差劲的手艺、严重的损害或强烈的愿望。

normal.en: The comparative is worse, like the adjective.
normal.cn: 比较级与形容词一样是 worse。

normal.en: Badly hurt and badly damaged are very common pairs.
normal.cn: badly hurt 与 badly damaged 是常见搭配。

normal.en: Want something badly means want it very much.
normal.cn: want something badly 意为非常想要。

normal.en: Badly does not mean 'in a bad mood'.
normal.cn: badly 并不表示「心情不好」。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: BAD-ly.
normal.cn: 重音在第一音节。

abstract.cn: 想象两只手紧紧攥着票。

examples.cn: 他非常想跑完这场比赛。

root: 由 bad 加 -ly 构成；bad 源自古英语，词源不明；副词由「以糟糕方式」引申出「严重地」与「非常」。

sensesIntro.en: Poor performance, severe damage and intense desire are one adverb in three strengths.
sensesIntro.cn: 做得糟、伤得重与想得厉害，是同一个副词的三档强度。

core.cn: 核心意象：一辆歪倒在路边的自行车。

definition_en: a soft container for carrying things, or to put something into one
core_image: 一只布袋鼓鼓地挂在椅背上
scene: 门口堆着刚买的东西。She packed the fruit into a paper bag.
sceneCN: 这里 bag 是「袋子」（第 1 个义项：用软材料做的容器）；句意是她把水果装进了一个纸袋。

derivatives.zh: 由 bag 加 -ful 构成，义为「一袋之量」
由 bag 与 -age 构成，义为「行李」
由 bag 加 -y 构成，义为「宽松的」

senses.title: A soft container
senses.definition: a container made of paper, cloth or plastic, open at the top
senses.definitionCN: 用纸、布或塑料制成、顶部开口的容器
senses.example: She packed the fruit into a paper bag.
senses.exampleCN: 她把水果装进了一个纸袋。
senses.why: Bag probably comes from Old Norse baggi, a pack or bundle, so the word began with the idea of a load carried together.
senses.whyCN: bag 可能来自古诺斯语 baggi「包裹、一捆」，所以这个词起初就有「把东西收在一起背着」的意思。

senses.title: A piece of luggage
senses.definition: a bag used for travel or for carrying personal things
senses.definitionCN: 旅行或随身携带物品用的包
senses.example: He left his bag at the hotel.
senses.exampleCN: 他把包落在了旅馆。
senses.why: A travel bag is simply the container sense narrowed to the things a person carries on a journey.
senses.whyCN: 旅行包只是把「容器」义缩小到旅途中随身携带的东西。

senses.title: To take or claim
senses.definition: to get or claim something, often before others
senses.definitionCN: 常指抢在别人之前拿到或占有
senses.example: They bagged the best seats by arriving early.
senses.exampleCN: 他们早到占到了最好的座位。
senses.why: Putting something into your bag is a concrete way of claiming it, which produced the informal verb sense.
senses.whyCN: 把东西装进自己的袋子，是占有它的具体做法，由此产生了口语里的动词义。

intro.en: Bag probably came from the Norse word for a pack.
intro.cn: bag 很可能来自诺斯语中表示「包裹」的词。

items.en: bag covered travel and shopping containers.
items.cn: bag 涵盖旅行与购物用的容器。

items.cn: 动词 bag 意为「装进袋子」。

items.en: Bag also means to claim something first.
items.cn: 如今 bag 也指抢先占得某物。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one vowel; the near-meaning group gives other containers.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个元音；近义组是其他容器。

normalIntro.en: A bag is a soft mouth that holds whatever you put in.
normalIntro.cn: bag 是一张柔软的嘴，装进什么就含住什么。

normal.en: The plural is bags, and the verb past is bagged.
normal.cn: 复数是 bags，动词过去式是 bagged。

normal.en: Pack a bag means prepare for a trip.
normal.cn: pack a bag 意为收拾行李准备出行。

normal.en: Bag a seat is informal for claiming a seat.
normal.cn: bag a seat 是「占座」的口语说法。

normal.en: Baggage is the uncountable word for all the bags.
normal.cn: baggage 是不可数的「行李」总称。

normal.en: The vowel is short: bag, not baag.
normal.cn: 元音是短音。

sensesIntro.en: A soft container, a traveller's bag and the act of claiming all begin with putting things inside.
sensesIntro.cn: 软容器、旅行包与占有的动作，都从「把东西装进去」开始。

definition_en: the bags and cases a traveller carries, or something heavy that weighs on the mind
core_image: 传送带上缓缓转来一只贴满标签的旧箱子
scene: 机场的转盘一直没有停。We waited by the belt for our baggage.
sceneCN: 这里 baggage 是「行李」（第 1 个义项：旅行时携带的箱包总称）；句意是我们在传送带旁等自己的行李。

senses.title: Luggage
senses.definition: the bags and cases that a traveller carries
senses.definitionCN: 旅行者携带的箱包总称
senses.example: We waited by the belt for our baggage.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在传送带旁等自己的行李。
senses.why: Baggage came from Old French bagage, a bundle of goods, so it named the whole load rather than one bag.
senses.whyCN: baggage 来自古法语 bagage「一捆货物」，所以它指的是整批行装，而不是单个包。

senses.title: Emotional burden
senses.definition: past experiences or feelings that weigh on a person
senses.definitionCN: 压在心上的过往经历或情绪

definition_en: to cook food in an oven with dry heat, or to become cooked this way
core_image: 烤箱里一盘面包慢慢鼓起来
scene: 厨房里飘出黄油的香味。She likes to bake bread on Sunday mornings.
sceneCN: 这里 bake 是「烘烤」（第 1 个义项：用烤箱的干热把食物烤熟）；句意是她喜欢在周日早上烤面包。

senses.title: To cook in an oven
senses.definition: to cook food with dry heat in an oven

senses.example: She likes to bake bread on Sunday mornings.

senses.why: Bake is an old English word that has always meant cooking with dry heat rather than over a flame.

senses.title: To become cooked

senses.why: If you can bake a thing, the thing itself can bake, which gave the word an intransitive sense.

definition_en: a steady state, the money left in an account, or to keep something steady
core_image: 天平两端各放一只砝码，指针缓缓停住
scene: 收银台前，店员抬头看了看屏幕。Please check the balance on your card.
sceneCN: 这里 balance 是「余额」（第 2 个义项：账户里剩下的钱）；句意是请查看你卡里的余额。

derivatives.zh: 由 balance 加 -ed 构成，义为「均衡的；平稳的」
由 im- 加 balance 构成，义为「失衡」
由 balance 加 -ing 构成，义为「平衡；权衡」

senses.title: Steady position
senses.definition: a state in which weight is evenly spread and nothing falls
senses.definitionCN: 重量均匀分布、不会倒下的状态
senses.example: She kept her balance on the icy path.
senses.exampleCN: 她在结冰的小路上保持着平衡。
senses.why: Balance came from Latin bilanx, 'two scales', so its first sense is the equal weighing of two sides.
senses.whyCN: balance 来自拉丁语 bilanx「两架天平」，所以最初的义项是两边等重。

senses.title: Money left
senses.definition: the amount of money remaining in an account
senses.definitionCN: 账户中剩余的钱数
senses.example: Please check the balance on your card.
senses.exampleCN: 请查看你卡里的余额。
senses.why: A scale shows what is left after amounts are set against each other, so the word came to mean the money remaining.
senses.whyCN: 天平会显示两边相抵后剩下的量，于是这个词就用来指账户中剩余的钱。

senses.title: To weigh or steady
senses.definition: to keep something steady or to compare two needs
senses.definitionCN: 使某物保持稳定，或比较两方面的需求
senses.example: You must balance study and rest.
senses.exampleCN: 你必须平衡学习与休息。
senses.why: Holding scales level became a verb, and from weighing objects it extended to weighing competing demands.
senses.whyCN: 把天平端平变成了动词，并从称量物件扩展到权衡相互竞争的需求。

definition_en: a small platform outside a building with a rail, or an upper seating area

senses.title: Outdoor platform

senses.title: A round mass

definition_en: unable to pay debts, or to make a person or company unable to pay

scene: 玻璃门上贴着一张价目表。The barber trimmed his hair in ten minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 barber 是「理发师」（第 1 个义项：以剪发为业的人）；句意是理发师十分钟就给他剪好了头发。

senses.title: A person who cuts hair
senses.definition: a person whose job is to cut and trim hair, especially men's hair
senses.definitionCN: 以剪修头发为业的人，尤指给男性理发者
senses.example: The barber trimmed his hair in ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 理发师十分钟就给他剪好了头发。
senses.why: Barber came from Latin barba, 'beard', because cutting beards was the original trade.
senses.whyCN: barber 来自拉丁语 barba「胡须」，因为修胡须本来就是这个行当的活。

senses.title: A barber's shop
senses.definition: the shop where a barber works
senses.definitionCN: 理发师工作的店铺
senses.example: He went to the barber's for a shave.
senses.exampleCN: 他去理发店刮了胡子。
senses.why: English often names a shop by its worker, so the barber's came to mean the barber's shop.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用店员的称呼来指店铺，所以 the barber's 就表示理发店。

intro.en: Barber goes back to the Latin word for a beard.
intro.cn: barber 可追溯到拉丁语中表示「胡须」的词。

items.en: barba meant 'a beard'.

items.en: barbier named a man who cut hair.
items.cn: barbier 指给人理发的人。

items.en: barber kept the trade sense.
items.cn: barber 保留了这一行业含义。

items.en: barber also means a barber's shop.
items.cn: 如今 barber 也可指理发店。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the barb- opening; the near-meaning group gives hair trades.
note.cn: 形近组都以 barb- 开头；近义组是美发行业的说法。

definition_zh: 赤裸的；光秃的；勉强的；露出
definition_en: not covered by clothes or anything else, or only just enough
core_image: 冬天的树枝光秃秃地伸向天空
scene: 雪化了，院子里一片安静。The trees stood bare against the sky.
sceneCN: 这里 bare 是「光秃的」（第 2 个义项：没有叶子或覆盖物）；句意是树木光秃秃地立在天空下。

pos.zh: 形容词：赤裸的；光秃的；勉强的

derivatives.zh: 由 bare 加 -ly 构成，义为「几乎不；仅仅」
由 bare 加 -ness 构成，义为「赤裸；荒芜」
由 bare 加 -ing 构成，义为「露出」

senses.title: Not covered
senses.definition: not covered by clothes or a covering
senses.definitionCN: 没有被衣服或覆盖物遮住的
senses.example: He walked on the sand in bare feet.
senses.exampleCN: 他赤脚走在沙滩上。
senses.why: Bare is an old English word for 'uncovered', and the body is its most direct subject.
senses.whyCN: bare 是古英语中表示「没有遮盖」的词，身体是它最直接的对象。

senses.title: Empty or leafless
senses.definition: without leaves, furniture or other usual covering
senses.definitionCN: 没有叶子、家具或其他常见覆盖物
senses.example: The trees stood bare against the sky.
senses.exampleCN: 树木光秃秃地立在天空下。
senses.why: A surface with nothing on it is uncovered in the same way as skin, so bare describes empty branches and rooms.
senses.whyCN: 表面什么都没有，和皮肤没被遮住是同样的「空」，所以 bare 也形容光秃的树枝与空荡的房间。

senses.title: Only just enough
senses.definition: no more than the minimum needed
senses.definitionCN: 不超过所需的最低限度
senses.example: They had the bare minimum of food.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的食物仅够最低需要。
senses.why: If nothing extra covers a thing, only the essential remains, which produced the sense of a bare minimum.
senses.whyCN: 如果没有多余的东西覆盖，剩下的就只有必需部分，于是产生「最低限度」的义项。

intro.en: Bare is an old English word for 'uncovered'.
intro.cn: bare 是古英语中表示「没有遮盖」的词。

items.en: baer meant 'uncovered or naked'.
items.cn: baer 意为「没有遮盖的、赤裸的」。

items.en: bar kept the sense of being uncovered.
items.cn: bar 保留了「无遮盖」的含义。

items.en: bare described empty land and rooms.
items.cn: bare 形容空旷的土地与房间。

items.en: bare minimum meant only what is needed.
items.cn: bare minimum 意为仅够所需。

items.en: barely means hardly at all.
items.cn: 如今 barely 意为几乎不。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one sound; the near-meaning group gives uncovered and plain.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个音；近义组是裸露与朴素的说法。

root: 源自古英语 baer「没有遮盖的、赤裸的」；由身体无衣引申为树木无叶、房间无物，再引申为「仅够最低限度」的用法。

sensesIntro.en: Uncovered skin, empty branches and the minimum left are three degrees of nothing extra.
